conventions.convention: Cell modules are right modules. The cell law has coefficients independent of the first tableau index, modulo the span of strictly higher shapes.
Multipartition dominance compares cumulative sizes of earlier ordered components plus row-prefix sums in the current component; strict dominance excludes equality.
The anti-involution is R-linear word reversal fixing every T_i and X_j, including inverse generators; it is not the semilinear bar operator.

The initial tableau fills components in order and rows consecutively. The right entry action is t·w = w⁻¹·t, and d(t) satisfies t^λ·d(t) = t. Murphy elements use the row symmetrizer and the factors ∏_{c=2}^r ∏_{i≤a_c}(L_i−u_c).
For composition and multicomposition fillings, d(t) denotes the extended unique tableau permutation; row-standardness supplies its minimal row-coset property.
Cell actions and forms commute with commutative scalar extension; radicals are recomputed after specialization and need not commute with arbitrary scalar extension.
Ordinary Specht label λ corresponds to the sign twist of the row-Murphy cell at λ′; no untwisted same-label identification is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: Over R_A = Z[Q±1], the standard type-A Murphy elements form a basis, reversal exchanges their tableau indices, the dominance spans are two-sided ideals, and right multiplication satisfies the dominance cell law with coefficients independent of the first index. The proof does not divide by Q+1 or assume semisimplicity.

For a composition α of n and row-standard α-tableaux s,t, every nonzero coefficient in the unique integral standard-Murphy expansion of m^α_st has output tableaux u,v dominating s,t at every label and row cutoff, and output shape μ dominating the sorted composition ᾱ. These identities specialize to every commutative ring with unit Hecke parameter.

Row-standard multicomposition Murphy elements straighten to standard cyclotomic Murphy elements with each output component partition dominating the sorted input component, the respective component assignments preserved, and both tableau-prefix inequalities preserved. Finite-generator multiplication satisfies the fixed-first-index law modulo strictly higher multipartition shapes.

The displayed adjacent component-shift identity, componentwise finite-generator straightening, and component-coset expansion give two-sided dominance ideals and an X_1 multiplication law whose same-shape terms preserve the first tableau index modulo strictly higher shapes.

The standard cyclotomic Murphy elements form an R-basis of H_{r,n}, satisfy m_st* = m_ts, and obey the dominance cell law for every h with coefficients independent of s. The dominance spans are two-sided ideals. The basis and cell law survive every commutative base change without specialized semisimplicity or inversion of quantum integers.

For a cellular algebra over a commutative ring with finite cell poset, the coefficient action defines unital right cell modules. Same-cell multiplication defines a unique symmetric bilinear form satisfying ⟨xa,y⟩ = ⟨x,ya*⟩, and its radical is a right submodule.
